runs.text: Before we can begin our study on justification by faith, we must first explain several Bible words. These words are “justification” and “sanctification”. The biblical words justification and sanctification each have companion terms that mean the same thing. The companion synonym words will be our definitions.
Justification =
dikaioma 1345

The Greek word dikaioma is interpreted once as justification, and is also interpreted 4 additional times as righteousness. Justification means righteousness. So, when we see the word “justification”, it means righteousness.
Strong’s Concordance defines
dikaioma
as “that which has been deemed right as to have force of law”. What this means is that justification = “righteousness of the Ten Commandment law,” or “perfect righteousness”.
Sanctification =
hagiasmos
The Greek word
hagiasmos
is interpreted 5 times as sanctification but also an additional 5 times as holiness. What this means is that in the Bible, sanctification and holiness are used interchangeably.

We also notice below that the word holiness in Romans 6:22 is combined with “fruit”. This explains how the process of holiness (sanctification) works. Holiness is when the [Fruit of the Spirit] is seen in our lives.
Romans 6:22
But now being made free from sin, and become servants of God, ye have your
fruit
unto
holiness,
and the end everlasting life
(Sanctification will be studied in Lesson #3, “
Walking in the Spirit
We have just learned that:
1. Justification, righteousness, and the Ten Commandments law are all connected.
2. Sanctification, holiness, and fruit are used interchangeably.
By using their synonyms, we now know the definition of “justification”, and “sanctification”.
SIN ENTERED THE WORLD:
1. How did death spread into the world?
Romans 5:12
Therefore, just as through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men, because all sinned.
Note:

When Adam and Eve fell, they could not have foreseen that their children would be tainted with the effects of sin. From that point forward, Adam’s descendants became bent towards self, causing all to sin, deserving death.
THE DEFINITION OF SIN:
2. What is the definition of sin?
1 John 3:4
Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for
sin is the transgression of the law.
Note:
Sin is the transgression of God’s law.
3. What must be present before there is trans-gression?
Romans 4:15
Because the law worketh wrath: for
where no law is, there is no transgression.
Note:
Sin cannot exist unless there is transgression of God’s law. This is because sin is breaking God’s law.
PENALTY FOR SIN IS DEATH:
4. What are the wages of sin?
Romans 6:23
For the wages of sin is death;
but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Note:
The penalty for breaking the law is death!
5. What did God tell Adam would happen if he ate from the forbidden tree?
Genesis 2:17
but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat,
for in the day that you eat from it you will surely die
Note

: Adam broke God’s direct commandment and came under the dominion of the second death. (The first death is the death that all suffer. The second death is what happens to the unforgiven sinner after the judgment.) (See Revelation 22: 12-14)
WHAT IS GOD’S REMEDY FOR SIN AND DEATH?
6. What did God offer that would reign through eternal life and righteousness?
Romans 5:21
That as sin hath reigned unto death,
even so might
grace
reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.
Note:

God’s answer to the sin problem is grace! God’s grace offers man a way out of the death penalty for breaking God’s law. This solution restores righteousness to the sinner so that the sinner could once again receive eternal life. God’s plan is to restore by faith the righteousness required by the law.
GRACE -VS- THAT STUMBLING-STONE:
7. How should Israel have obtained justification?
Galatians 3:10
For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them. 11
But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.
Note:
To become justified, we need to live by faith. We receive righteousness as a
free gift
from God
8. How did Israel try to attain to the law of righteousness?
Romans 9:31
But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness.
Wherefore? Because
they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone
Note:

Israel followed every letter of the law of righteousness. They thought of themselves as so righteous in their law-keeping that they feared that touching an unclean thing would defile them, but at the same time, they were plotting the death of an innocent man.

Mankind is broken! We generally cannot see the depth of our own perversion because of sin. There is more to the righteousness of the law than just keeping the letter of the law. True righteousness has to come from the heart. But first, we need to see our brokenness. If we fail to see our brokenness we will never search for true righteousness. True righteousness is seen in the life of the Son of God. Works of the law without faith in Christ is that stumblingstone.
FREE GARMENT OF SALVATION:
9. What was Isaiah covered with?
Isaiah 61:10
I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God;
for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness.
(See Zechariah 3:4)
Note:

We receive righteousness as a free gift. We are covered with it like a garment when we believe in Jesus as our savior. The way this works is: when we believe in Jesus, the righteous life of Christ is then credited to our account. From that moment onward, when God looks at our life, He sees a perfect, sinless life. This is because we are covered with the robe of Christ’s righteous life. In effect, God rewrites our history so our sin no longer exists.
10. What does it mean to put on Christ?
Galatians 3:24
Wherefore the law was our school-master to bring us unto Christ,
that we might be justified by faith.
For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
Note:
Justification is the robe of His righteousness that is placed on the believer. Strong’s Concordance says, to “put on” means to “sink into clothing”.
11. Who is Christ?
John 3:16
For
God
so loved the world, that he
gave his only begotten Son
, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
Note:
Jesus is God’s son. 1 John 5:12
He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life
. God sent His son to redeem us!
JUSTIFICATION IS BY FAITH:
12. What type of gift does Christ give us?
Romans 5:18
Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so
by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life
Note:
Justification means our life record now shows a history of a perfect righteous life. Because of Jesus’ sinless life we can have His
free gift
of righteousness. The plan of salvation is the restoration of believers to the righteousness of God. It is a free gift!
13. Who gives us this gift of righteousness?
Romans 5:17
For if by one man’s offense death reigned by one;
much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.
18 Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so
by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life.
Note:
In Adam, death reigned in us. But the gift of righteousness shall also reign by one man, Jesus Christ. Righteousness is a gift, a free gift!
14. Do our works contribute to the free gift?
Romans 4:3
For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.
Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. 5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.
6 Even as David also describeth
the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works.
Note:

We are NOT justified by faith plus works. We are justified by faith alone. To him that worketh not, but believeth on Him, his faith is counted as righteousness. Any believer who has tried to add his or her own good works as a contribution to their justification will forfeit salvation altogether! (See Galatians 5:4)
BELIEVING:
15. Why did God give His only begotten Son to save us?
John 3:16
For
God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
Note:
The basis for our salvation is the love of God. This love is demonstrated in God’s gift of His Son. God freely gives salvation as a gift to all who believe in His Son.
16. What did Jesus say would happen to those who believe in God and Jesus whom He sent?
John 5:24
Verily, verily, I say unto you,
He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me
hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.
Note:
Can we know for certain that we are saved? The Bible makes it plain that if we believe, we HAVE passed to everlasting life. It does not say that we will pass to life in the future! (See 1 John 5:13)
17. What happens to those who do not believe on Jesus?
John 3:36
He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and
he that believeth not the Son shall not see life
; but the wrath of God abideth on him.
Note:

To have eternal life we must know for certain that we believe on the Son of God. The words “hath”, and “believeth” are in the present tense. It means that we can hold it in our hands! He that believeth not, shall not see life. If we do not know for certain that we have believed, it is because we are in a state of unbelief. There is only one requirement to be justified, we MUST exercise faith in God’s ability to do what He says He will do. This requires us to stop our unbelief!
18. What is the requirement for a person to be saved?
Acts 16:31
And they said,
Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved,
and thy house.
Note:

We must believe on the Lord Jesus Christ. Yet there are some professed Christians who only partially believe. I partially believe when I believe that God saves sinners, but I do not believe that God saved me! I must stop my unbelief and enter into salvation through faith in the Lord!
SHEEPFOLD:

19. In this parable, Jesus compared those who believe in Him to sheep. The sheepfold in Jesus’ time was a stone fence where the shepherd kept his sheep. What did Jesus say about those who try to enter the sheepfold without going through the door?
John 10:1
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.
Note:
There is only one door to salvation. Those who try to enter through a different way than through the door are a thief and a robber.
20. Who does Jesus say is the door of the sheep?
John 10:7
Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep
Note:

We enter the sheepfold through Christ. He is the door. Anyone who tries to enter through a different door may come with good intentions, but in reality, they rob themselves of their assurance of salvation in Christ.
If Jesus is the door, then the sheep enter through belief in Him. If we enter through belief, then it stands to reason that the only way to exit from the sheepfold is through unbelief!

Many enter through belief in Christ, but then because they do not “feel like they are saved”, or they do not see good works in their flesh, they stop believing and begin doubting. Doubt is unbelief. If you doubt because you do not “feel like you are saved”, then in all reality you must have believed because you at one time “felt saved”.
Anyone who bases their salvation on emotions has entered the sheepfold through feeling instead of entering through the door which is Christ
. They are not conscious of the fact that they have entered through a different door which makes them a thief and a robber. This is how unbelief robs us of the assurance of salvation!
OLD AND NEW TESTAMENT:
21. What clear statement does the Old Testament make concerning the just, — those who have accepted the righteousness of Christ?
Habakkuk 2:4
Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him:
but the just shall live by his faith.
Note:

This Old Testament verse is quoted three times in the New Testament. (Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11, Hebrews 10:38) The righteousness of the Patriarchs in the Old Testament was by faith. (See also Romans 4:1-5)
22. In contrast to the Old Testament, how did the New Testament Gentiles obtain righteousness?
Romans 9:30
What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith
Note
: “The just shall live by his faith” applies to all people across all ages. Both the Old, and New Testament confirm, righteousness is by faith in Christ.
23. What did it cost the apostle Paul, who was a Jew and a Pharisee before his conversion, to obtain the righteousness of God that comes by faith?
Philippians 3:8.
I count all things but loss
for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom
I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ,
And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith.
Note:

It is impossible to be saved by faith in Christ and still hold on to our own righteousness as a means of saving ourselves. We are saved by justification by faith in Christ alone. So while we are not saved by faith plus works, genuine justification by faith will always produce good works (fruit) as evidence of our salvation. (See Ephesians 2:8-10) But we must remember, that any good works that God produces in us are not our works. They are produced by God and we cannot claim them as our own.
24. What happens when a believer tries to add works of the law as a contribution towards justification by faith?
Galatians 5:4
Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.
Note:

Any believer who has tried to add his or her own good works as a contribution to their salvation, will forfeit salvation altogether! So by accepting the righteousness of Christ, we must admit our own total depravity. Thus we cannot add our own good works, which falsely implies that our flesh is good. The gospel will not allow salvation partly of Christ, and partly of us. Yes, the true Christian will reflect the love of Christ, seen as good works. (See James 2:17) But these loving works are the result of seeing the love of God who saved us. (See Romans 2:13, 15)
25. What was the central doctrine of the Protestant Reformation?
Romans 1:16
F
or I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth
; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. 17
For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
Note:
Martin Luther was a Protestant reformer who lived in the 16th century. He is credited with restoring the doctrine of justification by faith alone to the Christian church.
Justification by faith alone (
sola fide

) was a central issue in Martin Luther's Ninety-Five Theses and his broader critique of the Catholic Church. In 1517, Luther challenged the Church’s practices, particularly the sale of indulgences, which he saw as implying that salvation could be bought or earned through works.
His theses, nailed to the Wittenberg church door, argued that salvation comes through faith in God’s grace alone, not through human efforts or Church rituals.
Luther’s emphasis on
sola fide
stemmed from his study of Scripture, especially Romans 1:17, which states, “
The just shall live by faith

.” He believed the Church’s focus on indulgences, penance, and works undermined the gospel’s core truth. He taught that justification by faith in Christ alone is the sole means for the forgiveness of our sins.

The doctrine of justification by faith alone was so vital during the Protestant Reformation that many chose to face death by being burned at the stake rather than renounce their faith in Christ’s free gift of salvation. We invite you to pause and contemplate this profound gift from God.

Our heartfelt prayer for those exploring the Good News of the Everlasting Gospel is that you, too, may find the conviction to hold fast to your faith in this divine gift, even at the cost of your life.
